description: How organisations run on information systems and sell through electronic channels, with mobile money and African fintech as a first-class case rather than a footnote. Taught to the depth of a leading management information systems and e-commerce course.
modelledOn: Laudon and Laudon, Management Information Systems
Laudon and Traver, E-commerce: Business, Technology, Society
Turban, King, Lee, Liang and Turban, Electronic Commerce
Bank of Ghana payment systems and mobile money guidelines
outcomes: Classify information systems by level and function and explain how they support decisions.
Map a business process and show how an ERP or workflow system automates and integrates it.
Compare e-commerce business and revenue models and design a payment flow including mobile money.
Explain how CRM and customer data create value and the privacy duties that come with them.
Align an information systems strategy with organisational strategy and evaluate it with ROI and total cost of ownership.
Build and present a small e-commerce prototype with a payment integration in sandbox mode.

units.title: Information systems in organisations
topics: Data, information, knowledge; systems thinking; input, process, output, feedback
Types of information systems: TPS, MIS, DSS, EIS, knowledge work and office systems, expert systems
Functional systems: finance, HR, marketing, operations; cross-functional integration
Information systems in Ghana: GhIPSS, the national ID, e-government portals, hospital systems
Hardware, software, data, networks, people and procedures as the components of a system

units.title: Business processes and ERP
topics: Business process modelling with flowcharts and BPMN; swimlanes; as-is and to-be
Order-to-cash and procure-to-pay processes
Enterprise resource planning: modules, a single database, integration benefits and implementation risks
Supply chain management systems and the bullwhip effect
Business process re-engineering and change management; ERP in SMEs with open-source options

units.title: E-commerce models
topics: B2C, B2B, C2C, B2G, m-commerce, social commerce; marketplaces versus own stores
Revenue models: sales, subscription, advertising, transaction fee, affiliate, freemium
The e-commerce value chain: catalogue, cart, checkout, fulfilment, returns
Case studies: Jumia, Tonaton, Hubtel and informal commerce on WhatsApp and Instagram

units.title: Payments
topics: Card payments: issuers, acquirers, networks, authorisation, settlement, chargebacks
Payment gateways and processors; PCI DSS; tokenisation
Digital wallets, bank transfers, QR codes, buy-now-pay-later
Payment security: 3-D Secure, fraud detection, strong customer authentication

units.title: Mobile money and fintech
topics: How mobile money works: agents, float, wallets, USSD and apps, interoperability (GhIPSS, MMI)
M-Pesa, MTN MoMo, Telecel Cash and AirtelTigo Money: history, scale and economics
Fintech services: lending, savings, insurance, remittances; the e-levy debate
Regulation: Bank of Ghana payment systems rules, KYC/AML, agent networks
Integrating a mobile-money API into an application in sandbox mode
Fraud and consumer protection in mobile money

units.title: Customer data and CRM
topics: Customer relationship management: operational, analytical and collaborative CRM
Customer lifetime value, segmentation, loyalty programmes, churn
Digital marketing: SEO, search and social advertising, email, analytics and conversion funnels
Personal data, consent and Ghana's Data Protection Act applied to customer data

units.title: Information systems strategy
topics: Linking IS strategy to business strategy; Porter's five forces and value chain; competitive advantage from IT
Build versus buy versus subscribe; cloud, SaaS and outsourcing decisions
IT governance: COBIT and ITIL in brief; roles of CIO and IT steering committees
Digital transformation and platform strategies; data as an asset
Information systems planning and portfolio management

units.title: Evaluation and ROI
topics: Costs: capital, operating, hidden; total cost of ownership
Benefits: tangible and intangible; measuring productivity and the productivity paradox
ROI, NPV, payback period and break-even for IT investments; a worked business case
Post-implementation review and benefits realisation

units.title: E-commerce project
topics: Building a small online shop with a catalogue, cart, checkout and sandbox payment
Security, trust and legal requirements: terms, privacy policy, receipts
Logistics and fulfilment in Ghana: addressing (GhanaPostGPS), delivery, cash on delivery
Presenting the business case and a demonstration

schedule.title: Systems thinking and types of information systems
schedule.exercise: Draw a systems diagram of a school fees office showing inputs, processes, outputs and feedback, and say which type of information system each part is.

tasks.title: Draw an input-process-output-feedback diagram for a pharmacy stock system, labelling data, information and the feedback loop
Match eight business scenarios to TPS, MIS, DSS, EIS or expert system and justify each choice from the decision type involved
Draw a cross-functional diagram of how a sale flows through marketing, finance, operations and HR in a small trading company and mark integration points

schedule.title: Information systems in Ghana
schedule.exercise: Write a short comparison of two national information systems in Ghana, covering users, data held, risks and benefits.

tasks.title: Draw an architecture diagram of a hospital information system showing hardware, software, data, network, people and procedures
Assess a case study of an e-government portal rollout, identify three failure risks and choose a mitigation for each
Design a small relational table structure for a national ID lookup service, run lookups on 20 sample records, and write a query that flags duplicate identities

schedule.title: Business processes and ERP
schedule.exercise: Model the current and improved order-to-cash process for a small distributor and list the steps you would automate.

tasks.title: Draw a BPMN swimlane diagram of an as-is order process with customer, sales and warehouse lanes
Model a procure-to-pay process in BPMN with an approval gateway for purchases above 5000 cedis and mark the control points
Decide which ERP modules and implementation approach suit a case-study manufacturer and score the plan on cost, risk and integration benefits

schedule.title: Supply chains and process change
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page change plan for introducing a new inventory process in a small shop, covering training and resistance.

tasks.title: Simulate weekly orders along a four-stage supply chain with SQL tables and show the order variability increasing upstream
Evaluate an ERP change-management case, identify why staff resist, and choose the training and communication steps that score highest
Draw to-be process diagrams that remove two bottlenecks in an as-is process, and compare cycle time and handoffs before and after

schedule.title: E-commerce models
schedule.exercise: Compare a marketplace seller, a WhatsApp shop and an own website for a clothes seller, with revenue, cost and risk of each.

tasks.title: Classify 10 online businesses as B2C, B2B, C2C or B2G, and as marketplace or own store, with a reason for each
Pick the revenue model for three start-ups from sales, subscription, advertising, fees or freemium, and defend it with unit economics
Model the e-commerce value chain from catalogue to returns for a local online grocer and identify the step with the highest drop-off

schedule.title: Online payments
schedule.exercise: Draw the path of a card payment from checkout to settlement, naming each party and what it contributes.

tasks.title: Draw the authorisation and settlement flow of a card payment with issuer, acquirer and network, and mark where a chargeback enters
Store card tokens instead of numbers in a payments table, run queries that only touch tokens, and show what an attacker with the table would see
Review fraud signals in a scored scenario of 12 transactions, set rules for 3-D Secure challenge, and balance fraud loss against lost sales

schedule.title: Mobile money
schedule.exercise: Explain how a mobile money cash-in, transfer and cash-out work in terms of agents, float and the ledger, with an example amount.

tasks.title: Record cash-in, transfer and cash-out in a wallet ledger table with SQL and verify that the sum of all wallets equals the agent float
Compare the economics of two mobile money providers in a case study, choose a fee structure and justify its effect on adoption
Evaluate a proposed micro-lending product built on mobile money, set eligibility and interest rules, and score its risks to borrowers

schedule.title: Regulation, APIs and consumer protection
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page checklist for launching a mobile money integration, covering KYC, limits, consent and dispute handling.

tasks.title: Decide KYC tier, daily limit and agent rules for a new wallet in a scenario and justify each against the regulatory rubric
Diagram the sequence of calls for a sandbox payment: request, customer prompt, callback and confirmation, marking where retries must be idempotent
Respond to a mobile money fraud case with evidence, choose freeze, reversal and customer communication steps, and be scored on protection and speed

schedule.title: Customer relationships and digital marketing
schedule.exercise: Design a loyalty programme for a pharmacy chain and say how you would measure whether it works.

tasks.title: Write SQL to segment 200 customers by recency, frequency and spend and list the top and at-risk segments
Compute customer lifetime value and churn rate by segment from a purchases table and recommend which segment to retain
Handle a case where a shop wants to use customer phone numbers for marketing, apply data protection principles, and be scored on consent and minimisation

schedule.title: IS strategy, sourcing and governance
schedule.exercise: Write a recommendation memo on whether a polytechnic should build, buy or subscribe to a student records system.

tasks.title: Apply Porter's five forces to a case-study retailer, identify where IT gives advantage, and choose the system investment that scores highest
Decide build, buy or subscribe for three systems in a case study, scoring cost, control, risk and local support
Draw an IT governance structure showing the steering committee, CIO and the review path for a new project proposal

schedule.title: Digital transformation and planning
schedule.exercise: Draft a three-year IS plan for a regional bank branch network, listing projects in priority order with reasons.

tasks.title: Assess a platform strategy for a delivery start-up, identify the data assets, and choose which to share and which to protect
Plot six candidate projects on a value versus risk portfolio chart and diagram the delivery roadmap in a Gantt chart
Choose which of eight proposed IS projects to fund under a budget limit, and defend the choice in a scored planning scenario

schedule.title: Costs, benefits and business cases
schedule.exercise: Complete a business case for a point-of-sale system for a chain of shops, with costs, benefits, ROI and payback period.

tasks.title: Tabulate capital, operating and hidden costs of a system over five years in SQL and compute total cost of ownership
Identify tangible and intangible benefits in a case study, assign values where defensible, and explain why productivity gains may not appear
Compute NPV, payback period and break-even for an IT investment from yearly cash flows and show how the decision changes at a 20 percent discount rate

schedule.title: Building and presenting an online shop
schedule.exercise: Prepare a five-minute demonstration and business case presentation for your online shop, with a rehearsed answer to two hard questions.

tasks.title: Design tables for products, customers, orders and payments in SQL, place three orders and check stock decreases correctly after each
Review an online shop case for missing terms, privacy notice and receipts, and be scored on which legal and trust items are fixed
Plan delivery for an online order in Ghana with address capture, rider cost and cash on delivery risk, and choose the option with best margin
